issue_context.title: Double check UPDATING.md for "2.0" doesn't include breaking changes in import paths
issue_context.body:
Hello, 

We should check if all operators and hooks available in Airflow 1.10 are also importable in Airflow 2.0. All these changes should also be included in
https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/master/tests/deprecated_classes.py

Technically speaking, we should install Airflow 1.10, generate a list of operators/hooks, and then try to import each of it on Airflow 2.0.
In order to generate a list of operators, we can use this script:
https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/master/scripts/list-integrations.py

If anyone is interested in this task, I am willing to provide all the necessary information.

Are you wondering how to start contributing to this project? Start by reading our [contributor guide](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.rst).

Best regards,
Kamil Breguła
comments: I would like to take this up, would give me a head start with 2.0
@bhavaniravi I assigned you to this ticket.

@mik-laj I have a question 

How does `deprecated_classes` handle backward compatibility when importing modules instead of classes 

Example:

```
from airflow.contrib.hooks import gcp_kms_hook"
```
Instead of 
```
from airflow.contrib.hooks.gcp_kms_hook import GoogleCloudKMSHook
```

@bhavaniravi We have two deprecation messages. One for the module and one for the classes. When it comes to use it for Python it makes no difference if you import the entire module and use the class referencing, as attributes, or import each class in your modulle.
@bhavaniravi are you still working on this?

Do we need to anything more here? Is this issue for core operators / AIP-21 ?

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/master/UPDATING.md#changes-to-import-paths
As I was checking, all imports worked.

review_comments:
This import is not valid. We do not expect users to import BaseHook by:
```
from airflow.hooks.filesystem import BaseHook
```
BaseHook should be imported at all times, as shown below.
```
from airflow.hooks.base_hook import BaseHook
```
There is a broken backwards compatibility here, but we can't prevent API misuse as Python is too flexible
All these have not changed either.
